newsitem.title: USA: NY gas utilities told to file "fixed-price option".
newsitem.headline: NY gas utilities told to file "fixed-price option".

text.p: The New York State Public Service Commission said the state's major gas utilities, with the exception of New York State Electric & Gas Corp, have been directed to submit proposals to provide a "fixed-price option" beginning with the next heating season.

This option, sought in response "to significant fluctuations in the price of natural gas last winter," would allow customers to lock in a fixed price per unit of gas consumed, the commission said in a statement.

It said NYSEG is exempt from the requirement because it already operates under hard price caps for its residential customers and has been offering a fixed-price option for non-residential customers since 1995.

The statement said it is also the commission's belief that utilities should re-evaluate the current practice of purchasing all supplies that track a relatively volatile pricing index such as the New York Mercantile Exchange.
With that in mind, the commission said, it directed the utilities to review their overall gas procurement.

It said the utilities affected are Brooklyn Union Gas Co, Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Corning Natural Gas Corp, Long Island Lighting Co, National Fuel Gas Co, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc, Rochester Gas & Electric Corp and St. Lawerence Gas Co Inc.
The commission said they will have 60 days from the time the commission issues its formal written decision to submit plans for offering a fixed-price option.

The regulators said the option contemplated would be designed as an interim measure for use during the current transition to a more open market where competitive providers are expected to offer packages of services that include a fixed price option.
The commission said it determined it will review the issue in two years as comptition continues to evolve.
